sources.citation: OLAC combined catalogue, 'OLAC resources in and about the Rungtu Chin language' (rtc), the Internet Archive 2023 copy.
sources.note: No language description listed. Only: Bernot 1968 Pangloss/CoCoON tape (birman [yaw], thaungtha, bande 069 A/B), Glottolog and Ethnologue records. Alt. names: Central/Northern/Southern Rungtu, Thaungtha.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds). 2016. Ethnologue, 19th ed., entry 'Chin, Rungtu' (rtc). SIL International. (Internet Archive copy)
sources.note: Nothing. Dialects Northern/Central/Southern Rungtu (94-96% within, 60-66% with Rawngtu [weu]); Typology: 'SOV; negation is marked after the verb'; unwritten; population 5,000 (2015 Language and Social Development Organization).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (Ethnologue Editor). 2011. Change Request Number 2011-016: adopted create [rtc] Rungtu Chin. SIL International. 5 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Records only that Rungtu shares ~60% lexical similarity with Rawngtu Chin and that 'Sociolinguistic research was conducted by Myanmar researchers in 2008.. wordlists and leader interviews' (p. 4); 'Knowledge from published sources' left blank.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2010. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3 [rtc] (companion form to CR 2011-016). SIL International. 3 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Gives autonym Rungtu, alt. name Taungtha, location 'Htilin Township and Kyaukhtu (Saw) Township within Magwe Division', classification Kuki-Chin Southern, closest language Rawngtu; 'Knowledge from published sources' blank; literature 'none'; unwritten.

sources.citation: Bernot, Denise. 1968. Fonds Denise Bernot, birman [yaw], taungtha, bande 069, faces A and B (audio wordlist and sentences). Pangloss / CoCoON, LACITO-CNRS.
sources.note: The only archived audio of Taungtha; would allow a first-hand instrumental look at word prosody, though it carries no written analysis.

sources.citation: Grierson, G. A. (ed.). 1904. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III, Pt. III: Tibeto-Burman Family, Specimens of the Kuki-Chin and Burma Groups. Calcutta. 'Southern Chin sub-group', pp. 329-330, plus the Taungtha column (W. B. Tydd) in the comparative vocabulary.
sources.note: Nothing. 'We have very little information with regard to the dialects spoken by these tribes'; Taungtha ('an industrious race who inhabit the Yaw and Myittha valleys') represented only by Tydd's vocabulary and a numeral table; 'Chinbok and Taungtha seem to be akin to Sho' (pp. 329-330). Identity: this Yaw-valley Taungtha = the Rungtu area.

sources.citation: Scott, J. George & J. P. Hardiman. 1900. Gazetteer of Upper Burma and the Shan States, Part I, Vol. I. Rangoon. Chin vocabularies, p. 682 ff. (Taungtha and Chinbok lists supplied by W. B. Tydd).
sources.note: Nothing. 'Taungtha and Chinbok were supplied by Mr. W. B. Tydd' (p. 682); a bare wordlist with no phonological notes.
Nothing. Entry retired to Bookkeeping with no justification text; the reference search for 'Rungtu' returns exactly one item, the ISO change request; 'Taungtha' returns none.

sources.citation: Wikipedia (en) 'Rungtu language'; Wikipedia (en) 'Taungtha people'; Wikipedia (my) 'ရုန်းတူဘာသာစကား' and 'တောင်သားလူမျိုး'.
sources.note: Nothing; the only linguistic references cited are Ethnologue, the ISO change request and Grierson 1904 (plus a Payap thesis on K'chò, a different language).

sources.citation: Language and Social Development Organization (LSDO) / SIL Myanmar researchers. 2008 (data), c. 2015 (revision). Sociolinguistic survey of the Rungtu (Taungtha) Chin, Htilin and Kyaukhtu townships: wordlists and leader interviews. Unpublished (cited in ISO 639-3 CR 2011-016 and as Ethnologue's 2015 population source).

sources.note: The only field data on Rungtu named anywhere; a survey wordlist could at least show whether the transcribers marked tone/stress. Publication was 'delayed because of local sensitivities'.

sources.citation: Any Myanmar university MA/PhD thesis or MAAS research-journal paper on the Taungtha (တောင်သား) language of Htilin/Saw (Burmese-language; existence not confirmed).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Burmese-medium theses on unrecognised Magway groups are the most likely place a phonology of Rungtu would exist; no catalogue reachable by automated download lists one.

sources.citation: Catalogue searches with zero relevant hits for 'Rungtu' / 'Taungtha': Crossref, CiNii (Latin and katakana), J-STAGE, MAAS (Myanmar Academy of Arts and Science) journal site in English and Burmese, archive.org catalogue. OpenAlex, Google Books API, Semantic Scholar and scholar.archive. SIL.org, ELP, live Ethnologue, HathiTrust, BASE and every web search engine could not be reached by automated download.
